The paper's reference [33] is the Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Measures Package edition (item 1 'On the whole, I am satisfied with myself', negatively worded items 2,5,6,8,9), not the socy.umd.edu order (item 1 'person of worth', negatives 3,5,8,9,10). (6) THE ANCHORS ARE FLIPPED ON FIVE ITEMS, deliberately, against those value labels. The live resp is stored ALREADY REVERSE-CODED: all 45 inter-item correlations are positive (min +0.32), alpha over the stored values is .898 against the published .90, and the raw column sum equals the published total (39.124/6.951 vs 39.12/6.95) -- the deposit's own aggregate column `self_esteem` is that same raw sum. This is a deliberate override of a level-1 label (the baka2023_bpnsf / burkert_2019_whoqol_bref case): the labels were evidently left attached after the recode and are wrong-as-attached for the five negatives. One consequence: irw-validate may flag resp_ambiguous (two scale directions in one table); that flag is correct about the table and is the point of the flip. (7) DEVIATION FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION, disclosed: the RSES reproduction actually read (novopsych PDF, sha256 6bf63b95daa52e8dfe40b973c2803515bcc0edc7d970b73b0dd33ad96ed99d97) prints its ten items WITHOUT terminal periods; periods were added here to match the canonical rendering and the sibling table wang_2016_study1_se. Nothing else was altered. The paper's own English gloss of the scale, 'ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)', is NOT what ships -- the .sav's Chinese is the administered anchor wording and names all five levels, which the gloss does not. (8) COVERAGE: se3, se4 and se7 have no respondent at resp=1 (level counts 0/4/30/114/62, 0/1/24/112/73, 0/4/26/120/60); option rows are shipped for all five levels of every item anyway, which is over-coverage, not a gap.
